standard_prerequisites.name: Complete Sigma-consistent set
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set Gamma of formulas is Sigma-consistent when it does not prove falsity in the calculus with axioms Sigma, and complete when for every formula A either A or its negation belongs to Gamma.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both defining properties are used in every clause, most visibly in the negation case and in the consistency arguments (source lines 505-506, 533-536, 550-552).

standard_prerequisites.name: Deductive closure
standard_prerequisites.statement: Gamma is deductively closed in Sigma, so any formula provable from Gamma together with Sigma belongs to Gamma.
standard_prerequisites.use: The first clause proves deductive closure and the remaining clauses use it repeatedly to move from a proof to membership (source lines 532-537, 538-541, 546-548, 554-561).

standard_prerequisites.name: Tautological instances and their provability
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every tautological instance of a propositional schema is provable from Sigma, and combining such an instance with membership in Gamma yields further membership.
standard_prerequisites.use: Each connective clause invokes a specific tautological instance, for example the introduction and elimination schema for conjunction or the extraction schema for implication (source lines 554-561, 563-568, 570-579, 581-595).

core_obligations: Deductive closure and containment of Sigma: show that Gamma proves A only if A is in Gamma, by deriving a contradiction from A not in Gamma together with completeness; then show that every member of Sigma is in Gamma using deductive closure (source lines 532-541).
The two constants: derive that falsity is not in Gamma from Sigma-consistency, and that truth is in Gamma from deductive closure applied to the provability of truth (source lines 542-548).
Negation: show that the negation of A is in Gamma exactly when A is not, the left-to-right direction from consistency and the right-to-left from completeness (source lines 550-552).

The four binary connectives: for conjunction, disjunction, implication and biconditional, prove both directions of the membership equivalence using the appropriate tautological instance of the connective together with the already established deductive closure, containment of Sigma and negation clause (source lines 554-595).

proof_roadmap.step: Deductive closure and containment of Sigma.
Falsity is not in Gamma and truth is.
Negation mirrors membership by consistency and completeness.
Conjunction, disjunction, implication and biconditional, each by the corresponding tautological instance.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own proposition prop:ccs-properties at source lines 504-528: a complete Sigma-consistent set Gamma is deductively closed, contains Sigma, contains the truth constant but not the falsity constant, and its membership relation mirrors each propositional connective, that is, negation, conjunction, disjunction, implication and biconditional. The proof at source lines 530-597 is a long case-by-case verification with a uniform but non-trivial pattern. Each clause has to be derived from the two defining properties of Gamma, completeness and Sigma-consistency, together with the fact that certain schemas are tautological instances and hence provable in Sigma: for instance the conjunction case runs the argument in both directions using the tautologies (A and B) implies A, and A implies (B implies (A and B)), the disjunction case argues through the negations of both disjuncts, the implication case uses the tautologies that extract the antecedent and the negation of the consequent from the negation of the implication, and the biconditional case combines the two directions. The earlier clauses are then reused inside the later ones, and the ordering of the cases matters. No cross-chapter result is invoked inside the retained span.
